PREP_COMMAND: tools/restore-upstream.sh kawpowminer # then build the static dependency prefix -- see NOTES
NOTES: Additionally needs external/referencestochatgpt/kawpow-deps, a PREBUILT static prefix (boost/jsoncpp/ethash) produced by external/contrib/build-kawpowminer.sh -- so a clean rebuild is a ~40 minute two-stage job with a network fetch, which is why CLEAN_BUILD_SUPPORTED=NO is recorded rather than assumed. The upstream checkout carries THREE uncommitted local modifications; a revision pin cannot restore those, so the patch is extracted to .private/upstream-patches/ even though the component is disabled. The honest first-party replacement is symoneural-miner-core, which is incomplete -- see its ALGORITHM-GAP.md.

No rack row points here; Studio's GPU work goes through the API's own engines, not through this tree. It DOES have a scripted rebuild path -- tools/fork_render_ui.sh -- which an earlier draft of this registry denied. Buildable and disabled are different facts and both are recorded.

INSTALL_COMMAND: sudo install -m0644 ops/symoneural-api.service /etc/systemd/system/ && sudo systemctl daemon-reload
NOTES: The rack. Serves every /api/* route, owns the GPU lease, and spawns the llm and diffuse engines as subprocesses. `symoneural-api/` at the repository root is the RUNTIME FOLDER (a launcher and a README), not the source; the source is backend/.
The owner asked for the API to have its own runtime folder like the other runtimes rather than being reachable only as a module of the web stack.

14 subcommands including import-claude. Installed as a SYMLINK, not a copy: a copied launcher at ~/.symoneural-full/bin diverged from its source and nothing noticed for days.
The runtime behind the path-fragility ratchet. Its README carries the marker-walk rule: never count parents to find the repository root.

CLEAN_ROOM_FROM_PUBLIC_SPEC is claimed for the Keccak only, and it is claimed literally: the round constants are COMPUTED from the LFSR in FIPS PUB 202 Algorithm 5 rather than pasted from anyone's table.
DEFINED, not PRESENT. The repository's own four-level vocabulary (DEFINED/PRESENT/WIRED/VERIFIED) is what this row is written in.
